label: Enoch third-factor reply quantified: union bound, binary sharpness and hard-case concentration
summary: Issue #1586, analyst formulation with attribution deferred; no new source reading (Enoch 2010 §§5.1-5.3 and Street 2006 used only through the existing #651 claims). Reuse check: truth related on 69c528d9 found the #651 access comparison and hard-case controls, no prior quantitative result; #1585 Darwinian horns reused as context, #1063/#1584 Mathlib probability vocabulary reused (uniformOn, cond), #1584 product profile not needed since no independence is assumed. Certified: (1) on one common distribution, selection error mu{B!=F}<=e1 and factor/truth gap mu{F!=M}<=e2 give mu{B!=M}<=e1+e2 and agreement >=1-(e1+e2) for a probability measure, verdicts of any type, no independence (error-set inclusion plus subadditivity); (2) sharpness: for binary verdicts {B!=M} is the symmetric difference of the two error sets, so mu{B!=M}+2mu(both)=e1'+e2' for the actual rates, attained iff the overlap is null; coinciding binary errors cancel; (3) a subclass gap is bounded only by the aggregate gap divided by the subclass weight; (4) four-case models: sharp 1/4+1/4 -> 1/2, cancelling 1/4,1/4 -> 1, and B=F with a 1/4 gap on the impartial hard case giving aggregate agreement 3/4 (attained) but 0 on the hard case. Semantic finding: Enoch's qualified pro tanto goodness of survival supports at most the one-way inclusion F -> pro tanto reason, so it bounds neither direction of the all-things-considered gap nor the reverse direction of the pro tanto gap; on impartial conflict cases (fitness-favoured option rejected by the realist's own impartial verdict) F and M diverge by the definition of the case class. Provisional judgment: the third factor gives a coherent quantified correlation for adaptive/self-regarding pro tanto targets; for impartial hard cases accuracy must come from the reasoning-from-starting-points mechanism Enoch adds (§5.1), whose reliability is a separate quantity not bounded by e1 or e2. Enoch's reply is not refuted: he claims only a modest correlation. Rejected: treating the aggregate bound as a per-case or per-subclass guarantee; deriving any value of e1 or e2 from the pro tanto premise; a chain bound through B and F as support for reflective hard-case verdicts. #1500 not linked: its premises concern kind/authority of reasons, not error rates. Informs #1506; no root premise change. Note docs/notes/third-factor-tracking-1586.md.
blocker: Empirical calibration of e1 and normative/empirical calibration of e2 per verdict type are open; the weight of impartial conflict cases in a realistic distribution and the reliability of reflective reasoning on them are open; graded (non-binary) verdicts, where errors need not cancel, are not covered.
